caption: Brendan Ngwa Nforbi v. AT&T Mobility Services LLC
court: USDC E.D. Cal. — Sacramento Division (proposed direct filing)
claims: FCRA § 1681b(b)(3)(A); ICRAA §§1786.40/1786.50; Penal Code §290.46(j)(2)(E)/(j)(4)(A) — v3 opening counts
status: FEDERAL REDRAFT v3 — E.D. Cal. Sacramento; narrowed to three statutory counts after hostile at-will/reliance audit. Contract/covenant/estoppel/misrepresentation reserved pending complete offer and reliance records.
note: Current source of truth is PR #802 v4 markdown complaint. Opening claims: FCRA adverse action, ICRAA adverse-action advice, and §290.46. No delayed-discovery date. Do not name Lerma in the complaint. Safeco willfulness is one paragraph, not a count. No REVIEW DRAFT banner on the caption. The prior contract/implied-covenant/promissory-estoppel/negligent-misrepresentation counts remain reserved. FADV report timing before 12:23 and LTI Spanish score/receipt timing are the decisive factual gates. Federal PDF generator is intentionally disabled until filing gates are cleared.
defendants: AT&T Mobility Services LLC, a Delaware limited liability company, is the proposed sole opening defendant as employer/user of the report and party to the May 28, 2026 written offer. AT&T Inc. is not named merely as parent. First Advantage Background Services Corp. is pleaded as AT&T's CRA from the May 28, 10:19 a.m. task (AT&T Non Management, account 132156) and remains a nonparty discovery source unless AT&T-specific records support an independent CRA claim. Richard Patterson and Orville R. Bell are witnesses, not presently named.
causes: [FEDERAL ANCHOR] FCRA §1681b(b)(3)(A) — I&B that AT&T based rescission in whole or part on a consumer report furnished before 12:23; no pre-adverse report/Summary of Rights; tangible accepted-job loss pleaded for Article III.
[STATE] ICRAA §§1786.40/1786.50 — I&B report obtained; no adverse-action advice identifying First Advantage; distinct omission from FCRA pre-adverse process.

[STATE] Penal Code §290.46(j)(2)(E)/(j)(4)(A) — I&B California-registry source/use; one-sentence same-consumer comparator; Plaintiff does not possess AT&T's report and does not allege source-field wording as known fact.
[RESERVED] FCRA §1681b(b)(2)(A) / ICRAA §1786.16 — inspect actual authorization package first.
[RESERVED] Contract, implied covenant, promissory estoppel, negligent misrepresentation — require complete offer/at-will/arbitration terms and concrete reliance/internal-score proof before addition.
[RESERVED] Fair Chance/FEHA, intentional fraud/concealment, First Advantage vendor claims — add only on independent prerequisites/evidence.
key_facts: On May 16, 2026, Plaintiff submitted two AT&T applications: R-107776 Retail Sales Consultant at Stockton Pacific and R-106742 Bilingual Spanish Retail Sales Consultant at Lodi. Both advanced through interviews. LTI provided an ACTFL Telephone OPIc Spanish test expiring May 25; the record still lacks the score, audio, threshold, receipt time, and decision notes. On May 28 at 10:13 a.m., Workday officially offered R-106742: Retail Sales Consultant reporting to Orville R. Bell at 2439 W. Kettleman Lane, $24.95/hour paid biweekly, $13,700 annual target variable compensation prorated for part-time hours, tentative June 15 start, candidate C-1690172. Contingencies omit Spanish. Workday issued onboarding tasks at 10:15–10:17 a.m.; First Advantage sent the AT&T Non Management screening task (account 132156) at 10:19 a.m. At 12:23 p.m., Patterson texted that the manager no longer wanted to proceed because Plaintiff did not pass Spanish. Plaintiff accepted through Workday, began onboarding, and received no pre-adverse report or rights summary. Report contents and use are I&B ultimate facts. No count uses a delayed-discovery date.
procedural_status: Pre-filing federal v3 on PR #802. Three opening statutory counts. Must audit First Advantage order/report/transmission timing and LTI Spanish score/AT&T receipt timing before filing. Confirm entity/SOS agent and use official federal forms.
damages: The offer confirms $24.95/hour, biweekly pay, a $13,700 annual variable-compensation target prorated for part-time hours, and a tentative June 15, 2026 start. It does not state weekly hours; those figures are not invented. Federal draft seeks nonduplicative actual/compensatory damages according to proof; FCRA remedies under §§ 1681n/1681o; ICRAA actual damages or $10,000, whichever is greater; Penal Code § 290.46(j)(4)(A) remedies; and contract/estoppel expectation or reliance damages. Portfolio valuation remains the post-favorable-MTD settlement range: $90,000 / $135,000 / $175,000. Do not plead § 1332 amount-in-controversy on invented LLC citizenship.
risk: Best current federal posture in the 36/37/39 set because all limitations clocks are fresh. Main merits risk: no proof yet that any consumer-report result was furnished before the 12:23 rescission; if none was, all three opening screening counts materially weaken. Second risk: AT&T's contemporaneous Spanish explanation could establish an independent disqualifier under Dutta if the score was received and automatically disqualifying. §290 remains source-specific; Lerma controls if the actual AT&T report contradicts registry sourcing. At-will and reliance law make the former four employment-offer fallback counts weaker, so they are reserved rather than used to dilute the opening complaint.
